english.title: Aircraft passenger interfere with performance of crew member - Air Navigation Order 2005
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) on **(..STATE FLIGHT NUMBER AND DEPARTURE AND DESTINATION AIRPORTS WHERE APPROPRIATE..) in an aircraft, namely **(..SPECIFY TYPE OF AIRCRAFT..), intentionally interfered with the performance by a member of the crew of the aircraft of

english.legislation: Contrary to Articles 78(c) and 148(6) of, and Part B of Schedule 14 to the Air Navigation Order 2005 made under sections 60 and 61 of the Civil Aviation Act 1982.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
This CJS Code and Standard Offence Wording is now OBSOLETE. Superseded by the Air Navigation Order 2009.

(i) See Articles 149 and 150 respectively of this Order for details of the extra-territorial effect of the Order when the aircraft is UK registered or when it is foreign registered but over UK territorial waters.
(ii) See the Civil Aviation (Amendment) Act 1996, which amends Section 92 of the Civil Aviation Act 1982, for when the aircraft on which the offence is committed is foreign registered and over foreign territorial waters.
